Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Naogaon and another
full_judgment:
2. The facts giving rise to the issuance of the Rule in a nutshell can be stated thus, the present petitioner as plaintiff instituted the original Other Class Suit No.66 of 1998 in the Court of learned the then Sub-ordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Naogaon against the defendant-opposite party for declaration of title in respect of 'Ka' schedule property contending inter alia that the suit property appertaining to Mouza Hajinagar under Neyamatpur police station of District-Naogaon corresponding to C.S. khatian No.107 and S.A. khatian No.2, 88 and R.S. khatian No.1 in C.S. plot No.733, 212, 176 and present plot No.1145, 82 and 123 comprising an area of 3.60 acres of land originally belonged to Koibara Estate. The Zamindar of the said estate while owning and possessing the suit property transferred 0.18 acres of land out of 2.43 acres of C.S. plot No.733 in favour of one Krishna Mohon Fouzdar and the remaining portion of the 'Ka' schedule land was settled in favour of the plaintiff in the year 1351 B.S. at a 'Najar' of Tk.105/- (one hundred and five). The plaintiff paid rent to the Zamindar and obtained 'dakhila'. Subsequently, while the land vested upon the government the plaintiff paid rent to the government `seresta' and the S.A. 107/5 attested khatian was prepared in the name of plaintiff and thereafter, during R.S. operation the land has been correctly prepared in the name of the plaintiff in field `bujarat' khatian No.632. Subsequently, while the khatian was finally prepared in the name of defendant No.2 the plaintiff filed an Objection Case being No.195/1972, which was allowed on contest on 22.10.1972. The legal heirs of Krishna Mohon Fowjdar by a transfer deed dated 08.04.1997 sold out his 18 decimals of land of 'Ka' schedule in favour of the plaintiff and the sub-kabala was registered in Neyamatpur Sub-registry Office. In this way, the plaintiff after acquiring the entire 'Ka' schedule property use to possess the same and on 09.07.1998 the Union Land Office declined to accept rent from the plaintiff, disclosing that the property-in-dispute has become khash property under the government and the government will settle the land. Thereafter, on 19.08.1998 on getting the certified copy of the khatian, the plaintiff came to know that the suit property has been wrongly recorded in the name of government, which constrained the plaintiff to institute the original suit for declaration of title. 

 3. The contrary case of the government in short is thus, that the suit is not maintainable and barred by limitation and the same is bad for defect of parties. The further case of the government-opposite party is such that during R.S. operation the land has been correctly recorded in the name of government as khash land as the land is under the "Shyrat Mohol" and in the remark column of the khatian, it has been cited that the property is being used by the people of the locality at large from the very beginning, using the water of the suit property for their agricultural purposes and the plaintiff having no manner of right, title, interest and possession in the suit property on the basis of false allegation filed the suit. 

 8. The learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the learned Appellate Court during disposal of the appeal committed gross illegality and irregularity. The learned Advocate further submits that the learned court of appeal below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice, by not considering that the plaintiff obtained settlement of the suit land on 27th Magh of 1351 B.S. and the settlement paper has been properly proved by the plaintiff which has been marked as Exhibit-1. The subsequent Vakhilas' were also proved and marked as Exhibits-2-2(Ga). The learned Advocate also submits that the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Naogaon without rebutting the findings of the trial court adverting evidence on records, reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial court illegally and in passing the impugned judgment and decree there has been misreading and non reading of evidence and non-consideration of material facts resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned counsel argued that the property-in-dispute had been correctly recorded in the name of plaintiff-petitioner in the field `bujarati khatian No.632 during the preparation of R.S. record of right and subsequently, the suit land have been wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No.2 and against that wrong record the plaintiff filed an Objection Case being No.195 of 1972 before the concerned settlement officer and the settlement officer on hearing both the parties allowed the objection Case No.195 of 1972 on 22.01.1972 A.D. vide Exhibit-5 and accordingly the government after acceptance of rents granted rent receipt in favour of the plaintiff vide Exihibit-6 and the learned appellate court was totally misconceived in appreciating the documentary evidences adduced from the plaintiffs side, which has been marked as Exhibits-1-8. The learned Advocate lastly submits that the government admitting the plaintiffs tenancy right to the suit property recognizing the plaintiff a tenant under government, granted rent receipt after accepting rents and the learned trial court after proper evaluation of the evidence on records conclusively held that the plaintiff has successfully discharged his onus of proof, but the defendants have hopelessly failed to disprove the case of the plaintiff and there is no evidence excepting the attested photocopy of the R.S. khatian No.1 marked as Exhibit-'Ka' from the side of the government to justify their case that the property has been vested to the government and the R.S. record of right has been rightly prepared, but the learned appellate court during disposal of the appeal without proper sifting of evidence in its true perspective and without proper appreciation of law, arbitrarily decided the merit of the appeal in favour of the appellant and passed the impugned judgment and decree, which is liable to be set aside. 

 10. In order to appreciate the argument advanced from the sides of the learned counsels for the respective parties, on perusal of the impugned judgment and decree dated 25.08.2011 and the judgment and decree passed by the trial court in Other Class Suit No.66 of 1998, the evidence led from the sides of the respective parties and all other relevant papers including the case records it transpires that, admittedly the disputed property described in schedule `ka' of the plaint originally belonged to `Koibara Estate' and it is the pleading's case of the plaintiff that the Zamindar of the said estate from the C.S. plot No.733 settled 0.18 acres of land out of 2.43 acres of land in favour of one Krishna Mohon Fowjdar and in respect of the remaining land of schedule 'Ka', the Ex-Zamindar settled that land in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner on 27th Magh of 1351 B.S. The Zamindari papers have been produced from the side of the plaintiff, and these documents support the plaintiff's pleadings case and these papers after its formal proof under the Evidence Act, have been marked as Exhibit-1-2(Ka) and 2 (Ga) respectively. From the said Zamindari papers, it transpires that the Zamindar after accepting rent from the plaintiff granted rent receipts of their `Koibara Estate'. I also find from the documentary evidences adduced from the side of the plaintiff that the R.S. attested khatian No.107/5 was prepared in the name of plaintiff marked as Exhibit-3 and the papers relating to Objection Case No.195/1972 (Exhibit-5), the relevant attested khatian No. 632 and 107/5 in the name of the plaintiff-petitioner and the government rent received including the information slip relating to the positive contention of the plaintiff, go to show that the right to the plaintiff-petitioner in respect of the suit property has been accepted by the government-opposite party and all the official papers definitely have a presumptive value under the ambit of section 114(e) of the Evidence Act, 1872. Besides this, it is also apparent from the rent receipt granted in favour of the plaintiff by the government that the government after accepting the rents from the plaintiff in respect of the suit property is now stopped from challenging the plaintiff's tenancy and it appears that, all these papers were properly evaluated by the trial court at the time of disposal of the Other Class Suit No.66 of 1998. 

 12. P.W.1 the plaintiff Kanai Lal in his testimony testified that he is the plaintiff to the suit and at a stage of his testimony he has categorically testified that, initially the draft S.A. khatian was prepared in his name and the S.A. attested khatian No.107/5 was prepared in the name of him and the field 'bujarat' khatian No.632 was also prepared in his name and subsequently while he came to know that the khatian has been finally published in the name of the defendant No.2, he filed an Objection Case being No.195/1972 which was allowed on contest and there has been an order from the office of the settlement officer that a khatian will be opened in his name (the plaintiff). The plaintiff in his deposition categorically testified that the legal heirs of Krishna Mohon Fowjdar after the death of Krishna Mohon transferred the land measuring 18 decimals in favour of the plaintiff-petitioner vide a registered sub-kabala deed dated 08.04.1997, which has been marked as Exhibit-8. During cross-examination from the side of the defendants, P.W.1 replied in a question that the property-in-dispute is never used by the people of the locality as `Shyrat Mohol, rather; the suit property is being used by him since his settlement. With regard to the boundaries of the suit land, P.W.1 Kanai Lal categorically testified about the boundary men, who are in possession in their lands, besides the suit land. 

 16. Vis-à-vis; the one and only witness of the defendant, D.W.1 Md. Abdul Mazid in his testimony testified that he is an Assistant Tahshildar of Hajinagar Union Land Office. He has brought the R.S. record book, wherefrom it appears that the suit property has been entried in khash khatian No.1. He has submitted the attested R.S. khatian which has been marked as Exhibit-'Ka'. During cross-examination D.W.1 in a reply to a question from the side of the plaintiff, testified that he has brought no paper showing that the suit land was ever possessed by the government through lease. D.W. 1, the concerned official witness of the government-opposite party in his testimony frankly admitted that the government rent receipt which has been produced from the side of the plaintiff, was issued by the government.
